task: Build the first horizon of adops v1: the demo shop loads end-to-end (adops init --demo, docker compose up, adops run Syncs orders/customers into the Postgres Warehouse) with 100% line+branch coverage and Docker E2E in CI.

analysis.objective: Ship v1 of Agentic DataOps (`adops`) — an Apache-2.0, uv-packaged Python CLI/library that scaffolds a user's Project (`adops init` / `adops init --demo`) whose YAML Pipelines (Sync via dlt for Verified Sources and PyAirbyte for Docker-free Community Sources, Transform via dbt, Reverse Sync to databases with Preview) are validated and compiled to Dagster, run against Postgres or DuckDB Warehouses across dev/stage/prod and Branch Environments, and are operated by the user's own Assistant through an MCP server and six skills with GitOps Promotion via GitHub Actions — so that a SQL-literate user with no Git or Docker knowledge can operate it.
analysis.successDefinition: v1 is done when ALL hold: (1) installing the `adops` package yields a working `adops` CLI; `adops init` and `adops init --demo` scaffold a Project with pipelines/, a dbt project, Environment settings, docker-compose.yml, `.env.example`, the 6 SKILL.md skills and GitHub Actions workflows — no tool code copied into the Project. (2) In a demo Project, `docker compose up` starts the demo shop Postgres (Source), the Postgres Warehouse and the Dagster metadata Postgres (+ optional Grafana/OTel profile), and `adops run` executes a Pipeline that Syncs orders/customers (Full Refresh and Incremental Sync), Transforms them with dbt models + tests, and Reverse Syncs a result into a Postgres database — writing only in stage/prod and producing a Preview in dev/Branch Environments. (3) The same Pipelines run unchanged on a DuckDB Warehouse. (4) Invalid YAML, missing Secret Reference, unreachable Source/Warehouse, empty Source table and a Breaking Change each produce a clear sanitized error; a Breaking Change halts the affected Step and downstream Steps. (5) Branch Environments are per-branch schemas in the stage Warehouse that defer to stage, rebuild only changed Steps + dependents, re-sync only when a Sync Step changed, and are dropped on merge/close. (6) Secret References resolve only from env vars/.env and no output/log/span/MCP response contains a secret value, asserted by tests. (7) The MCP server exposes edit/validate/test-connection/run/Preview/read-logs only for dev and Branch Environments, refusing stage/prod in server code. (8) The six skills check prerequisites, perform Git operations themselves and narrate plainly. (9) Generated GitHub Actions run PR→Branch Environment+tests, merge→stage, release/approval→prod. (10) The tool repo's CI enforces 100% line+branch coverage on `adops` package code and runs the demo end-to-end in Docker on every PR; every Verified Source passes the E2E suite. (11) Playbooks exist for Environments/Promotion and single-VM production. (12) No LLM key or Wren container is needed anywhere.
assumptions: confirmed: first slice = 'Demo shop loads end-to-end' — `adops init --demo` + `docker compose up` creates the shop Postgres (Source) and the Postgres Warehouse, `adops run` Syncs orders/customers into the Warehouse, with 100% line+branch coverage and CI (unit + Docker E2E) from day one; Transform, Reverse Sync, MCP, skills, Branch Environments, DuckDB, OTel and playbooks come later.
confirmed: Python with uv packaging, Apache-2.0, CLI name `adops`, Dagster run storage in a dedicated Postgres metadata container.
confirmed: production-grade bar — 100% line+branch coverage on `adops` package code enforced in CI plus end-to-end demo runs in Docker in CI.

GLOSSARY.md and ADR-0001–0011 override the production spec wherever they differ; the spec is background for invariants (AI proposes/deterministic code executes, no secrets to a model, quality gates readiness, explicit stream allowlists, sanitized errors).
Coverage is measured on the tool's own package code; scaffolded templates are validated by tests/E2E but not counted as Python coverage.
For Community Sources, PyAirbyte uses an explicit SQL cache pointed at the Warehouse — never the implicit default cache and never Docker-based connectors (ADR-0004/0012).
The v1 Verified Source set is Postgres (demo shop) plus CSV/Parquet files per the grilling session; every other PyAirbyte source is a Community Source.

Dagster is an internal implementation detail; users and the Assistant touch only Pipeline YAML and the `adops` CLI/MCP; Dagster run storage + PyAirbyte cache state replace the spec's custom run-state tables.
dev, stage and prod are separate deployments of the same tool (ADR-0001); in CI, stage can be simulated by a Postgres container.
External systems (PyAirbyte, dbt, Dagster, databases) sit behind project-owned ports so unit tests reach 100% branch coverage with fakes; real behaviour is proven by the Docker E2E suite.

confirmed: Verified Sources (Postgres, files) Sync through dlt; PyAirbyte only for Docker-free Community Sources, both behind one Sync port (ADR-0012) — because PyAirbyte 0.71.3 runs source-postgres only via Docker.
risks: dlt and PyAirbyte must both write to the Warehouse behind one Sync port with consistent raw-table naming and Incremental Sync state; divergence would make Community Sources behave differently from Verified ones.
Dependency conflicts between pinned PyAirbyte, dagster, dbt-core/dbt-postgres/dbt-duckdb and DuckDB could block a single uv lockfile.
100% branch coverage over heavy third-party integrations tempts over-mocking or `pragma: no cover` abuse — coverage met while E2E behaviour is untested.
Docker E2E runs in GitHub Actions may be slow or flaky, making the mandatory CI gate a bottleneck.

Branch Environment deferral needs stage dbt state and stage Warehouse access from CI — credential exposure in PR workflows (forked PRs must not get stage secrets); cross-schema defer must behave the same on Postgres and DuckDB.
DuckDB allows one writing process, so concurrent runs/Branch Environments on DuckDB can fail.
Secret values can leak via exceptions, connector/dbt logs, OTel attributes or MCP output; redaction must be central and tested.
The dev/Branch-only Assistant rule must be enforced in MCP server code; resolving the Environment from model-supplied arguments without validation would bypass it.
Reverse Sync idempotency/delete semantics on Postgres targets are hard; a wrong Preview diff would mislead users before a real write.
Breaking Change detection depends on schema-diff data PyAirbyte may not expose uniformly; false negatives let downstream Steps run on broken data.
Users without Git/Docker knowledge mean skills must handle missing Docker, busy ports and GitHub auth gracefully — hard to test automatically.
Scope is broad for one v1; without strict slicing the 100%-coverage bar may stall delivery.
outOfScope: Analytics Agent, Wren AI, Pydantic AI and the /ask skill — deferred to v1.1 by ADR-0010.
Multi-tenancy, tenant isolation, approval services, the enterprise security checklist and tenant-scoped API — ADR-0001 makes v1 single-team self-hosted.
Reverse Sync to SaaS destinations — ADR-0003 limits v1 to databases.
Warehouses other than Postgres and DuckDB — ADR-0004.
Docker-based Airbyte destination connectors (spec Pattern A) — ADR-0004.
End-to-end test coverage for Community Sources — only Verified Sources are in the CI E2E suite.
CDC Sync as a Verified path in the first slices — needs logical replication on the Source; the demo may show it later.
Vault or cloud secret-store plug-ins — ADR-0007 names them later work.
The Assistant acting directly on stage or prod — ADR-0009.
A web UI or hosted SaaS — ADR-0011 / ADR-0001.
CI/CD templates other than GitHub Actions — ADR-0009.
Multi-VM / Kubernetes / HA deployment and the spec's chaos/performance programme — v1 ships a single-VM playbook; Helm later.
Python-first Pipeline authoring beyond the escape hatch — ADR-0005.
Pydantic Logfire or vendor telemetry backends as defaults — OTel + optional Grafana only.
analysis.domainShapeReason: The objective carries DataOps rules a data-engineering expert recognizes (Reverse Sync writes only in stage/prod, a Breaking Change halts downstream Steps, the Assistant acts only in dev/Branch Environments, Promotion via Git), with real seams between Pipeline authoring/compilation, Environments and the Assistant interface.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: The user's own Git repository created by `adops init`, holding Pipelines, dbt models and Environment settings, separate from the tool package.
A version-controlled YAML definition of a chain of Steps that `adops` validates and compiles to Dagster.
An external system data is copied from; Verified Sources are covered by CI E2E, Community Sources are not.
A Step copying selected tables from a Source into the Warehouse — via dlt for Verified Sources, PyAirbyte for Community Sources — as Full Refresh or Incremental Sync, halting on a Breaking Change.
The analytical database (Postgres in docker-compose, or a DuckDB file) where synced and transformed data lives.
A Step copying Warehouse data back into an operational database; writes only in stage/prod, Preview elsewhere.
A fully separate place a Pipeline runs (dev, stage, prod, or a Branch Environment schema), between which changes move only by Promotion.
The env-var name of a secret used in configuration in place of its value; tools may report the name and whether it is set, never the value.
Writing and validating Pipeline YAML and Project settings (the rules a Pipeline must satisfy before it can run).
Resolving Secret References and running a valid Pipeline's Steps against a Warehouse, recording the run.
Creating a user's Project (plain or demo) from templates shipped in the tool package.
Packaging, locking, linting and CI gates of the adops tool itself (not the user's Project).

phases.name: Add uv package skeleton with coverage-gated CI
phases.goal: Create the installable `adops` Python package (uv-managed, Python 3.12, Apache-2.0) with one locked dependency set and a GitHub Actions workflow that fails any pull request whose `adops` package code is below 100% line and branch coverage.
phases.rationale: The repo is empty apart from docs, and every later phase assumes a package to put code in, a lockfile that resolves, and a CI gate that holds the coverage bar from the first line of code. Proving that dlt, Dagster and the Postgres driver resolve together in one lockfile is the main unknown and is cheapest to settle before any feature code exists.
changes: Write pyproject.toml with the hatchling (or uv_build) backend, `requires-python = ">=3.12"`, license Apache-2.0, and a `[project.scripts] adops = "adops.interface.cli:main"` entry point.

Declare runtime dependencies with pinned compatible versions: dlt[postgres], dagster, dagster-postgres, psycopg (binary), typer, pydantic v2, pyyaml, python-dotenv. Dev group: pytest, pytest-cov, dlt[duckdb] (tests only), ruff.
Run `uv python pin 3.12` and `uv lock`; commit uv.lock. If the resolver fails, adjust pins until it resolves and record the chosen versions.
Create the empty layer packages src/adops/{domain,application,infrastructure,interface}.
Configure coverage: branch = true, source = ["adops"], fail_under = 100, show_missing = true; exclude only `if TYPE_CHECKING:` — no other `pragma: no cover` allowed.

Add .github/workflows/ci.yml: on pull_request and push to main, a `unit` job using pinned actions/checkout and astral-sh/setup-uv, running `uv sync --locked`, `uv run ruff check`, and `uv run pytest tests/unit --cov --cov-report=term-missing`.
Add a trivial unit test (the package exposes `__version__`) alongside the CLI test.
Add a minimal Typer app in src/adops/interface/cli.py with `main()` and `adops --version`, tested with CliRunner, so the installed command works from day one; later phases add subcommands to it.
inputs: Pinned compatible dependency set (dlt, dagster, dagster-postgres, psycopg) proven with `uv lock` on Python 3.12
Pinned versions of actions/checkout and astral-sh/setup-uv
phases.expectedResult: The `unit` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml passes on a pull request, and fails when coverage of src/adops drops below 100% line+branch (checked by temporarily adding an untested branch).
phases.compensation: Revert the commit; nothing depends on it yet.

rubric.label: Locked install and working adops command
rubric.ruleStatement: A fresh clone installs from the committed lockfile on Python 3.12 and exposes a working `adops` console script with Apache-2.0 metadata. 10 = every bullet passes and `uv lock --check` proves the lockfile is current; 8 = installs and runs with only cosmetic metadata gaps; below 7 = install or entry point is broken.
passCriteria: `uv sync --locked` exits 0 on a clean checkout, and `uv lock --check` exits 0
`uv run adops --version` exits 0 and prints the same string as `uv run python -c "import adops; print(adops.__version__)"`
pyproject.toml has `requires-python = ">=3.12"`, an Apache-2.0 license field, and `[project.scripts] adops = "adops.interface.cli:main"`; `.python-version` contains 3.12
LICENSE holds the full Apache License 2.0 text (`grep -c "Apache License" LICENSE` >= 1 and the file is over 10 KB)
`uv tree` lists dlt, dagster, dagster-postgres and psycopg as runtime dependencies, with duckdb only in the dev group (`uv tree --no-dev | grep -i duckdb` returns nothing)
failureExamples: uv.lock is committed but stale, so `uv sync --locked` fails in CI after someone edited pyproject.toml
Plausible implementation: dlt[duckdb] is put in the runtime dependencies 'for convenience', so every user install pulls DuckDB even though it is only needed by the tests
`adops --version` prints a hard-coded string that differs from `adops.__version__`

rubric.label: 100% line+branch coverage gate truly bites
rubric.ruleStatement: Coverage is measured with branches on, over the adops package, fails below 100%, and cannot be bypassed with pragmas. 10 = the gate is proven to fail on an added untested branch, and the only exclusion is TYPE_CHECKING; 8 = configured correctly but the proof is manual; below 9 is unacceptable because every later phase relies on it.
passCriteria: pyproject.toml `[tool.coverage]` sets `branch = true`, `source = ["adops"]`, `fail_under = 100`, `show_missing = true`
`exclude_lines` / `exclude_also` holds only an `if TYPE_CHECKING:` pattern; `grep -rn "pragma: no cover" src/` returns nothing
Adding `if __import__('os').getenv('X'): pass` to src/adops/__init__.py makes `uv run pytest tests/unit --cov --cov-report=term-missing` exit non-zero (then revert)
`uv run pytest tests/unit --cov` on the delivered tree reports TOTAL 100% with zero missing branches
failureExamples: `fail_under = 100` is set but `branch` is left false, so a partial `if` passes the gate
Plausible implementation: `source` points at `src` or is omitted, so the measured set comes from imported modules only, and a never-imported module under src/adops is silently not counted
An `omit = ["*/interface/*"]` entry quietly removes the CLI from measurement

rubric.label: CI unit job is pinned, locked and blocking
rubric.ruleStatement: The workflow runs on pull requests and pushes to main, uses pinned actions, installs strictly from the lockfile, and fails the run on lint or coverage failure. 10 = actions pinned to commit SHAs with version comments and a pinned uv version; 8 = pinned to exact version tags; below 7 = floating refs or non-blocking steps.
passCriteria: .github/workflows/ci.yml triggers on `pull_request` and on `push` with `branches: [main]`
actions/checkout and astral-sh/setup-uv are pinned to an exact tag or a 40-char SHA (no `@main`, `@v4`-style major-only refs, or `@latest`)
The `unit` job runs `uv sync --locked`, `uv run ruff check`, and `uv run pytest tests/unit --cov --cov-report=term-missing` as separate steps
`grep -n "continue-on-error\|\|\| true" .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns nothing
`uv run ruff check` exits 0 locally on the delivered tree
failureExamples: Uses `uv sync` without `--locked`, so CI silently resolves new versions the lockfile never proved
Plausible implementation: pytest is run without `--cov`, relying on addopts that are missing, so coverage is never enforced in CI even though it is enforced locally
Actions referenced as `actions/checkout@v4` (major-only, mutable)

rubric.label: Four layer packages exist with CLI in the interface layer
rubric.ruleStatement: The domain, application, infrastructure and interface packages are importable, and the only code so far sits in the right layer. 10 = layers exist, the CLI lives only in interface, and domain/application import no third-party framework; 8 = layout correct with a minor stray import; below 7 = CLI or framework code in an inner layer.
passCriteria: `uv run python -c "import adops.domain, adops.application, adops.infrastructure, adops.interface"` exits 0
Typer is imported only under src/adops/interface: `grep -rln "typer" src/adops | grep -v interface` returns nothing
tests/unit/interface/test_cli.py exercises `adops --version` via typer.testing.CliRunner and asserts exit code 0
failureExamples: The CLI is placed in src/adops/__init__.py or src/adops/cli.py, outside the interface layer, so later phases wire commands into the wrong package
Plausible implementation: src/adops/__init__.py imports `adops.interface.cli` to re-export `main`, which makes importing the domain pull in Typer

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is a coverage config that looks right but does not bite (branch off, wrong `source`, or a stale uv.lock); fix it by setting `branch = true` and `source = ["adops"]`, re-running `uv lock`, and proving the gate with a temporary untested branch.

phases.name: Add Pipeline model and YAML validation rules
phases.goal: Define the pure domain types — Pipeline, Sync Step, Source, Warehouse, Environment and Secret Reference — and a function that parses Pipeline YAML and Project settings text into them, rejecting invalid input with clear, secret-free error messages.
phases.rationale: A Pipeline is a YAML file the user (or their Assistant) edits; everything downstream must be able to trust that it is already valid. Keeping these rules pure (no database, no environment variables, no file I/O beyond receiving text) makes them easy to test to 100% branch coverage and reusable by every later phase.
changes: Model a Pipeline (name, ordered Steps) and a Sync Step (name, Source name, explicit non-empty table allowlist, mode `full_refresh` or `incremental`) with pydantic v2 `extra="forbid"`.
Rule: an `incremental` table must declare `cursor` and `primary_key`; Step names unique within a Pipeline.
Model a `postgres` Source and `postgres` Warehouse whose password is a Secret Reference.
Model a Secret Reference as an env-var name (`password_env: SHOP_DB_PASSWORD`) validated with `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$`; it never holds a value.
Model an Environment (name, Warehouse, Sources) read from the Project settings file `adops.yaml`; only `dev` required in this slice.
Add `load_pipeline(text)` and `load_project_settings(text)` using `yaml.safe_load`, converting errors into one `PipelineValidationError` with `path: problem` lines that never echo raw field values.
Cross-check: every Sync Step's Source name exists in the chosen Environment.
inputs: GLOSSARY.md terms: Pipeline, Step, Sync, Full Refresh, Incremental Sync, Environment, Secret Reference
phases.expectedResult: src/adops/domain with `load_pipeline` / `load_project_settings`, covered 100% line+branch by tests/unit/domain, including tests for: unknown key, empty table list, incremental table without cursor, duplicate Step name, bad Secret Reference name, unknown Source name.

rubric.label: Domain stays pure (no I/O, env or framework imports)
rubric.ruleStatement: src/adops/domain depends only on the stdlib, pydantic and pyyaml, and receives text instead of reading files or environment variables. 10 = no forbidden import, no `open()`/Path reads, and a test or ruff rule enforces it; 8 = clean by inspection; below 9 is unacceptable for a domain layer.
passCriteria: `grep -rnE "^\s*(from|import) (os|dagster|dlt|psycopg|dotenv|typer|adops\.(application|infrastructure|interface))" src/adops/domain` returns nothing
`grep -rnE "open\(|environ|getenv|read_text|Path\(" src/adops/domain` returns nothing
`load_pipeline` and `load_project_settings` take `str` arguments (check the signatures in src/adops/domain/loader.py)
A ruff banned-api rule, an import-linter contract, or a unit test that walks the domain modules' imports enforces the ban (10 only)
failureExamples: `load_project_settings` accepts a path and calls `Path(path).read_text()`, pulling file I/O into the domain
Plausible implementation: the Secret Reference model gets a convenience `.is_set()` method using `os.environ`, which leaks an environment concern into the domain

rubric.label: Every validation rule has a rejecting test
rubric.ruleStatement: Each declared rule has at least one test that feeds invalid YAML and asserts the specific error path, and the domain is at 100% line+branch coverage. 10 = every rule plus malformed YAML and a non-mapping root are tested and asserted by error path; 8 = every listed rule tested; below 8 = any rule untested.
passCriteria: tests/unit/domain contains rejecting tests for: unknown key, empty table list, incremental table missing `cursor`, incremental table missing `primary_key` (separate test), duplicate Step name, Secret Reference name not matching `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$`, Step referencing a Source missing from the Environment, and mode other than full_refresh/incremental
Each test asserts the error's path (for example `steps[0].tables`), not just that an exception was raised
Malformed YAML and a YAML root that is a list/scalar each raise PipelineValidationError, not yaml.YAMLError or TypeError
`uv run pytest tests/unit/domain --cov=adops.domain --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing` reports 100% with no missing branches
`grep -rn "yaml.load(\|yaml.unsafe_load\|FullLoader" src/adops/domain` returns nothing
failureExamples: Tests only check `pytest.raises(PipelineValidationError)`, so a rule that fails for the wrong reason still passes
Plausible implementation: an empty YAML file returns `None` from safe_load and crashes with `TypeError` instead of a validation error

rubric.label: Validation errors never echo raw values
rubric.ruleStatement: PipelineValidationError is one exception with `path: problem` lines that never contain user-supplied field values. 10 = a sentinel test covers both pydantic and YAML-syntax errors and checks str, repr and args; 8 = sentinel tested for pydantic errors; below 9 is unacceptable because a mistyped password would leak.
passCriteria: A test puts a sentinel such as `LEAK-9f3a` as the value of an unknown key, an invalid mode and a bad `password_env`, and asserts the sentinel is absent from `str(err)`, `repr(err)` and `err.args`
A YAML-syntax error test asserts the message has no snippet of the offending line (yaml's `problem_mark` context is not copied)
Multiple problems in one document are reported together as several `path: problem` lines in one exception
The original pydantic/yaml exception is not chained (`err.__cause__ is None` and `err.__context__` is suppressed) so tracebacks cannot print it
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: the message is built from `str(pydantic_error)`, which includes `input_value='hunter2'` for each failing field
`raise PipelineValidationError(...) from exc` keeps the pydantic error as the cause, so a traceback still shows raw values
Only the first error is reported, forcing users to fix problems one at a time

rubric.label: Secret Reference stores only a variable name
rubric.ruleStatement: Credentials in Source/Warehouse models can only be given as Secret References (an env-var name), never as literal values. 10 = literal-password keys are rejected with a message naming `password_env`, and the model has no field able to hold a value; 8 = only name fields exist and `extra=forbid` rejects literals; below 8 = a literal password is accepted anywhere.
passCriteria: `password: something` in a Source or Warehouse block is rejected by `load_project_settings` (test exists)
The SecretReference model's only data field is the env-var name (inspect src/adops/domain/secret_reference.py)
Every pydantic model in src/adops/domain sets `extra="forbid"`: `grep -c "extra=\"forbid\"\|extra='forbid'" src/adops/domain/*.py` covers each model class
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: the model accepts `password_env` or `password` 'for local dev', so the demo works but secrets end up in Git
A nested Source model forgets `extra="forbid"`, so `pasword_env` (typo) is silently ignored and the run later fails with a confusing missing-secret error

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is error messages built from `str(ValidationError)`, which echo `input_value`; fix it by mapping each `err.errors()` entry to `".".join(loc): msg` with no `input`, and raising `from None`.

phases.name: Add run Pipeline use case with secret resolution
phases.goal: Add the application-level `run_pipeline` use case that takes Pipeline YAML, Project settings, an Environment name and a mapping of environment variables, resolves every Secret Reference, and hands the resolved run plan to an orchestrator port (default: an in-order runner) that executes each Sync Step through the Sync port.
phases.rationale: This is the single place that decides the order of work for `adops run`: validate, resolve secrets, then execute. Defining the Sync port (dlt now, PyAirbyte later) and the orchestrator port (an in-order runner now, Dagster in a later phase) here lets the adapters be built independently and lets this logic reach 100% coverage with in-memory fakes.
changes: Define the Sync port Protocol: `sync(step, source, warehouse) -> SyncResult` (rows loaded per table). ResolvedConnection holds the real password and masks it in `__repr__`/`__str__`.

Define the orchestrator port Protocol `execute(plan, sync) -> RunResult` and an `InOrderOrchestrator` default that runs Steps in Pipeline order, stops at the first failure and marks later Steps skipped.
Implement `resolve_secret_references(env, refs)`: return values or raise `MissingSecretError` naming every missing variable — names only, never values.

Implement `run_pipeline(pipeline_text, settings_text, environment_name, env, sync, orchestrator=InOrderOrchestrator())`: validate via the domain loader, pick the Environment (error if unknown), resolve Secret References, build the RunPlan, call `orchestrator.execute`, return RunResult.

Implement `run_pipeline(pipeline_text, settings_text, environment_name, env, sync, runner=None)`: validate via the domain loader, pick the Environment (error if unknown), resolve Secret References, build the RunPlan, call the orchestrator, return RunResult.
Unit-test every branch with fakes, including a test that no secret value appears in any error message or `repr()` of a resolved connection.
inputs: Domain loader and models from phase pipeline-model-and-validation
phases.expectedResult: src/adops/application/run_pipeline.py (with the Sync port) covered 100% line+branch by tests/unit/application using a fake Sync, including the missing-Secret-Reference, failing-Step-skips-later-Steps and secret-masking tests.

rubric.label: Application layer depends only inward
rubric.ruleStatement: src/adops/application imports only adops.domain, the stdlib and typing helpers, and gets environment values as a Mapping argument. 10 = enforced by an automated import check; 8 = clean by grep; below 9 = any outer-layer or framework import.
passCriteria: `grep -rnE "^\s*(from|import) (os|dagster|dlt|psycopg|dotenv|typer|adops\.(infrastructure|interface))" src/adops/application` returns nothing
`run_pipeline` takes `env: Mapping[str, str]`, and `grep -rn "environ\|getenv" src/adops/application` returns nothing
An import-linter contract, a ruff banned-api rule or a unit test enforces the ban (10 only)
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: `run_pipeline(..., env=None)` falls back to `os.environ` when env is omitted, which pulls process state into the use case
`ports.py` type-hints the Sync port with a dlt type such as `dlt.common.pipeline.LoadInfo`

rubric.label: Missing secrets reported all at once, by name only
rubric.ruleStatement: resolve_secret_references returns every value or raises one MissingSecretError naming all missing variables and no values. 10 = all missing names reported in sorted order, and the empty-string policy is explicit and tested; 8 = all names reported; below 8 = stops at the first missing name.
passCriteria: A test with two missing variables asserts both names appear in one MissingSecretError
A test with one set and one missing variable asserts the set variable's value is absent from `str(err)` and `repr(err)`
Behaviour for a variable set to an empty string is decided (missing or valid) and has a dedicated test
No secret is resolved and no Step runs when any reference is missing (the fake Sync records zero calls)
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: secrets are resolved lazily per Step, so Step 1 runs and loads data before Step 2's missing secret is reported
The error lists `KeyError('SHOP_DB_PASSWORD')` from a raw dict lookup instead of a domain error

rubric.label: Resolved secrets masked in every repr
rubric.ruleStatement: No object that holds or derives from a resolved secret shows the value in `repr`, `str`, or an exception message. 10 = a sentinel test covers ResolvedConnection, RunPlan, RunResult, SyncResult and every error raised; 8 = ResolvedConnection and errors covered; below 9 is unacceptable.
passCriteria: A test resolves a sentinel password and asserts it is absent from `repr()` and `str()` of ResolvedConnection and of the RunPlan that contains it
The same sentinel is absent from `repr(run_result)` and from the message of an error raised by a failing fake Sync
If ResolvedConnection is a dataclass, the password field uses `field(repr=False)` or `__repr__` is overridden; if pydantic, it uses `SecretStr` or an equivalent
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: ResolvedConnection overrides `__repr__`, but RunPlan is a plain dataclass whose auto-generated repr prints the nested connection's `__dict__` via a tuple of fields
An f-string in an error message such as `f"failed for {connection}"` uses `__format__` on a pydantic model that prints the raw field

rubric.label: Steps run in order; a failure skips later Steps
rubric.ruleStatement: The default runner executes Sync Steps in Pipeline order, stops at the first failure, marks the later Steps skipped, and returns a RunResult instead of raising. 10 = order, failed/skipped statuses, sanitized error and unknown-Environment error each tested with a recording fake; 8 = order and skip tested; below 8 = later Steps still run after a failure.
passCriteria: A recording fake Sync shows calls in Pipeline Step order for a 3-Step Pipeline
When Step 1 raises, the fake records no call for Steps 2-3, and RunResult reports Step 1 failed and Steps 2-3 skipped
An unknown Environment name raises a domain error naming the Environment and listing the available ones
`uv run pytest tests/unit/application --cov=adops.application --cov-branch` reports 100% with no missing branches
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: the runner catches the exception and `continue`s, so a failed customers Sync is followed by an orders Sync against an inconsistent Warehouse
RunResult reports later Steps as 'failed' instead of 'skipped', so the CLI cannot tell the root cause from its consequences

rubric.label: Sync port is engine-neutral
rubric.ruleStatement: The Sync port Protocol uses only domain and application types, so a PyAirbyte adapter can implement it unchanged. 10 = no engine terms in names or types, and the test fake is checked against the Protocol by a type checker or runtime_checkable test; 8 = neutral signature; below 7 = dlt concepts in the port.
passCriteria: `grep -nE "dlt|write_disposition|dataset|airbyte" src/adops/application/ports.py` returns nothing
SyncResult reports rows loaded per table as a plain mapping of table name to int
tests/unit/application/fakes.py implements the Protocol, and a test asserts `isinstance(fake, Sync)` with `@runtime_checkable`, or the type checker passes on it
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: the port method takes `write_disposition: str` because the dlt adapter needs it, so Full Refresh/Incremental leaks as dlt vocabulary instead of being read from the Step's mode

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is a secret leaking through an auto-generated dataclass repr of a container (RunPlan/RunResult) rather than ResolvedConnection itself; fix it by adding a sentinel test over every returned object and marking secret fields `repr=False`.

phases.name: Add dlt Sync adapter for Postgres Sources
phases.goal: Implement the Sync port with dlt so a Sync Step copies its allowlisted tables from a Postgres Source into a raw schema of the Warehouse, as Full Refresh (replace) or Incremental Sync (cursor + merge on primary key).
phases.rationale: dlt is the chosen engine for Verified Sources such as the demo shop Postgres because it is pure Python and needs no Docker socket. Wrapping it behind the Sync port keeps dlt details (pipeline names, state, write dispositions) out of the rest of the tool so PyAirbyte can sit behind the same port later.
changes: Build the dlt source with `sql_table` per allowlisted table, passing credentials programmatically from the ResolvedConnection (never via secrets.toml).
Full Refresh: `write_disposition="replace"`. Incremental Sync: `dlt.sources.incremental(cursor)`, `write_disposition="merge"`, `primary_key`.
Load into dataset `raw_<source name>`; name the dlt pipeline `adops_<pipeline>_<step>` so Incremental Sync state is stable across runs; keep dlt's working dir under the Project's `.adops/`.
Return SyncResult with rows loaded per table from dlt load info.
Translate dlt/database exceptions into `SyncFailedError` naming Step and table but stripping connection strings and passwords.

Test with real dlt and no Docker: SQLite Source → DuckDB destination, asserting Full Refresh replaces rows and a second Incremental Sync loads only advanced rows; map Warehouse kind to a dlt destination via a small function so tests can select DuckDB.
Postgres→Postgres behaviour (the real demo path) is proven by the Docker end-to-end test in phase run-command-and-demo-e2e; this phase's tests stay Docker-free.
inputs: Sync port and ResolvedConnection from phase run-pipeline-use-case
dlt sql_database source and Postgres/DuckDB destination docs for the locked dlt version
phases.expectedResult: src/adops/infrastructure/dlt_sync.py covered 100% line+branch by tests/unit/infrastructure/test_dlt_sync.py, with passing Full Refresh and Incremental Sync tests against SQLite→DuckDB.

rubric.label: Incremental Sync loads only advanced rows, no duplicates
rubric.ruleStatement: A second Incremental Sync run loads only rows whose cursor advanced, merges updates on the primary key, and reports only those rows as loaded. 10 = row count, the distinct-key check, the updated value and the reported delta are all asserted, and state survives a fresh adapter instance; 8 = count and no-duplicates asserted; below 9 is unacceptable.
passCriteria: The SQLite to DuckDB test inserts 1 new row and updates 1 row's cursor and a value, then runs again; afterwards `SELECT count(*)` equals original + 1 and `SELECT id FROM raw_<source>.<table> GROUP BY id HAVING count(*) > 1` returns zero rows
The updated row's new value is asserted in the destination
The second run's SyncResult reports exactly 2 rows for that table (not the full table count)
The second run uses a new adapter instance pointing at the same Project `.adops/` directory, proving dlt state persists under the stable name `adops_<pipeline>_<step>`
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: the test asserts only the final row count; it passes even though the cursor was never applied and all rows were re-read and merged, so the reported rows equal the full table
dlt's pipelines_dir defaults to ~/.dlt or a per-run temp dir, so Incremental state is lost and every run is a full reload
The merge has no primary_key, so the updated row appears twice

rubric.label: Full Refresh replaces the destination table
rubric.ruleStatement: A Full Refresh run makes the destination table equal the Source table, including deletions, inside the `raw_<source name>` dataset. 10 = deletes and updates both reflected, and the dataset name is asserted; 8 = replacement after a deletion asserted; below 8 = rows appended.
passCriteria: The test runs Full Refresh, deletes 1 Source row and updates another, runs again, and asserts the destination row set equals the Source row set
Tables land in schema/dataset `raw_<source name>` (asserted by querying DuckDB `information_schema.tables`)
Only allowlisted tables are loaded: a non-allowlisted Source table is absent from the destination
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: `write_disposition="replace"` is set on the source but overridden by a resource-level default of `append`, so a second run doubles the rows
The `sql_database` source is used without a table filter, so every Source table is copied, not just the allowlist

rubric.label: Credentials passed in memory; errors stripped of secrets
rubric.ruleStatement: Credentials go to dlt programmatically and are never written to disk, and every failure becomes a SyncFailedError naming the Step and table with no password or connection string. 10 = a sentinel failure test checks message, repr, the exception chain and the dlt working directory; 8 = message and repr checked; below 9 is unacceptable.
passCriteria: After a test run, `find <project>/.adops -name 'secrets.toml' -o -name 'config.toml'` returns nothing and `grep -r <sentinel> <project>/.adops` returns nothing

A test forces a connection failure with a sentinel password and asserts the sentinel and the `postgresql://` DSN are absent from `str(err)`, `repr(err)`, and from `err.__cause__`/`err.__context__` (raised `from None` or chain sanitized)
SyncFailedError's message names the Step and the table being loaded
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: `raise SyncFailedError(step, table) from exc`, where `exc` is a dlt PipelineStepFailed whose text contains the full DSN with the password, printed in any traceback
Credentials passed as a DSN string that dlt writes into the pipeline state/trace under `.adops/`

rubric.label: dlt confined to one adapter; tests Docker-free and fully covered
rubric.ruleStatement: dlt is imported only by the adapter module, which implements the Sync port and is 100% covered by tests that need no Docker. 10 = all bullets pass, including the Warehouse-kind-to-destination mapping for both postgres and duckdb; 8 = confined and covered; below 8 = dlt imported elsewhere or coverage under 100%.
passCriteria: `grep -rlnE "^\s*(import|from) dlt" src/adops` returns only src/adops/infrastructure/dlt_sync.py
`uv run pytest tests/unit/infrastructure/test_dlt_sync.py --cov=adops.infrastructure.dlt_sync --cov-branch` reports 100%
`grep -nE "docker|testcontainers" tests/unit/infrastructure/test_dlt_sync.py` returns nothing, and the test passes with Docker stopped
The destination-mapping function is tested for both `postgres` and `duckdb` and raises a clear error for an unknown kind
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: the Postgres destination branch is never executed in unit tests, so coverage is reached with a `pragma: no cover` on it
The application layer imports a dlt exception class to catch it, so dlt leaks out of infrastructure

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is that Incremental state is not persisted (pipelines_dir not pinned to the Project's `.adops/`), or the test only checks the final count; fix it by setting `pipelines_dir` explicitly and asserting both the no-duplicate GROUP BY and the reported 2-row delta on a fresh adapter instance.

phases.name: Add Dagster compiler and runner for run plans
phases.goal: Implement the orchestrator port with Dagster: compile a RunPlan into a Dagster job with one op per Step and execute it, recording the run in the Dagster instance configured for the Project (Postgres run storage in the demo).
phases.rationale: Dagster is the internal engine that runs and records Pipeline runs; users never write Dagster code. Keeping compilation and execution in one adapter behind the orchestrator port means the rest of the tool does not import Dagster, and later Step kinds only add op builders here.
changes: Add `compile_job(plan, sync)`: one `@op` per Sync Step calling `sync.sync(...)`, chained in Pipeline order; job name = Pipeline name.

Add `DagsterOrchestrator.execute(plan, sync)`: `DagsterInstance.get()` when `DAGSTER_HOME` is set, else `DagsterInstance.ephemeral()`; run with `execute_in_process(instance=..., raise_on_error=False)`.
Map Dagster step results to RunResult; a failed op marks later Steps skipped and surfaces the sanitized error, not the Dagster stack trace.
Pass resolved secrets to ops by closure, not run config, so they never reach Dagster run storage.
Unit-test with a fake Sync and an ephemeral instance: success path, failing first Step skipping the second, and stored run config containing no secret value.
inputs: Orchestrator port, RunPlan and RunResult from phase run-pipeline-use-case
Dagster docs for the locked version: programmatic jobs, execute_in_process, dagster_postgres run storage
phases.expectedResult: src/adops/infrastructure/dagster_orchestrator.py covered 100% line+branch by tests/unit/infrastructure/test_dagster_orchestrator.py, including the failing-Step-skips-downstream and no-secret-in-run-storage tests.

rubric.label: No secret value reaches Dagster run storage
rubric.ruleStatement: Resolved secrets reach ops only by closure, and nothing Dagster persists (run config, tags, event log, op outputs, failure events) contains a secret. 10 = a sentinel scan covers the run record, tags and every event for both a successful and a failing run; 8 = run config and event log scanned on success; below 9 is unacceptable.
passCriteria: A test runs with a sentinel password and asserts it is absent from `instance.get_run_by_id(run_id).run_config`, the run tags, and the str of every record in `instance.all_logs(run_id)`
The same scan passes for a run whose first op raises an error (the failure event's error info has no sentinel)
Ops do not return ResolvedConnection or any object holding the secret as an Output (inspect `compile_job` in src/adops/infrastructure/dagster_orchestrator.py)
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: run config is clean, but the op re-raises the Sync error and Dagster stores its full stack trace with local variables or the DSN in the STEP_FAILURE event
An op returns the plan's ResolvedConnection as an output, so its pickled value lands in the IO manager's storage

rubric.label: A failed op skips later Steps with a sanitized error
rubric.ruleStatement: When one op fails, later ops do not execute, RunResult marks them skipped, and the surfaced error is the sanitized adops message, not a Dagster stack trace. 10 = call recording, statuses, and absence of Dagster internals in the message all asserted; 8 = skip and status asserted; below 8 = later ops run or a raw trace surfaces.
passCriteria: With a recording fake Sync whose first call raises, the fake records exactly 1 call, and RunResult shows Step 1 failed and Step 2 skipped
`execute_in_process(..., raise_on_error=False)` is used, and `execute` returns a RunResult instead of raising
The RunResult error text contains the SyncFailedError message and no `dagster._core` or `Traceback` substring
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: ops are added without dependencies between them, so Dagster runs them in parallel or in any order, and Step 2 still runs after Step 1 fails
The error surfaced is `DagsterExecutionStepExecutionError` text with a nested traceback

rubric.label: Compiled job matches the Pipeline
rubric.ruleStatement: compile_job builds one op per Sync Step with names derived from the Step names, chained in Pipeline order, in a job named after the Pipeline. 10 = node names, dependency edges, and the handling of names that are invalid in Dagster are asserted; 8 = node count and order asserted; below 8 = shape untested.
passCriteria: A test asserts `job.graph.node_names` equals the Step names for a 3-Step plan
A test asserts each op N+1 depends on op N (inspect `job.graph.dependency_structure`)
`job.name` equals the Pipeline name; a Pipeline or Step name with a hyphen produces a valid Dagster name, or a clear error (tested)
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: every op is built from one shared `@op` definition with the same name, so Dagster raises a duplicate-name error once a Pipeline has two Steps

rubric.label: Correct Dagster instance chosen and the run recorded
rubric.ruleStatement: With DAGSTER_HOME set the adapter uses that instance and records the run in it; without it, it uses an ephemeral instance. 10 = both branches tested and the run record status asserted in a DAGSTER_HOME tmp instance; 8 = both branches tested; below 8 = only the ephemeral path exercised.
passCriteria: A test sets DAGSTER_HOME (via monkeypatch) to a tmp dir with a sqlite-backed dagster.yaml and asserts the run appears in `DagsterInstance.get().get_runs()` with SUCCESS status after `execute`
A test without DAGSTER_HOME asserts an ephemeral instance is used and nothing is written to the working directory
The adapter does not mutate `os.environ` (DAGSTER_HOME is read, not set, here)
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: `DagsterInstance.get()` is called unconditionally and the test suite passes only because a developer has DAGSTER_HOME set locally; CI then fails or writes into the home directory

rubric.label: Dagster confined to the adapter; orchestrator port stays neutral
rubric.ruleStatement: Dagster is imported only by the orchestrator adapter; the orchestrator port and run_pipeline use no Dagster types; and the default in-order runner still works. 10 = all bullets pass with 100% branch coverage of both changed files; 8 = confined with coverage met; below 9 = a Dagster import leaks inward.
passCriteria: `grep -rlnE "^\s*(import|from) dagster" src/adops` returns only src/adops/infrastructure/dagster_orchestrator.py
`grep -n dagster src/adops/application/*.py` returns nothing
The existing tests/unit/application tests still pass without passing an orchestrator
`uv run pytest tests/unit --cov --cov-branch` stays at 100%, including dagster_orchestrator.py and run_pipeline.py
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: the application layer imports `DagsterRunStatus` to map statuses, which ties the use case to Dagster

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is a secret reaching the STEP_FAILURE event through the re-raised exception's chain or message; fix it by raising only the sanitized SyncFailedError `from None` inside the op, and add an event-log sentinel scan for the failing run.

phases.name: Add adops init command for demo Project
phases.goal: Add the `adops` command-line app with an `init` command that writes a new Project into a target folder; with `--demo` it writes the demo shop Project: docker-compose.yml (shop Source Postgres seeded with customers/orders, Warehouse Postgres, Dagster metadata Postgres), adops.yaml, a Pipeline syncing orders and customers, dagster.yaml and .env.example.
phases.rationale: A user with no Docker or Git knowledge needs one command that produces a working Project holding only their files — no tool code is copied in. The demo Project is also what the end-to-end test runs, so its files must be valid by construction; a unit test loads the shipped Pipeline and settings through the domain validator.
changes: Add to the existing Typer app in src/adops/interface/cli.py the subcommand `adops init [PATH] [--demo]` copying the template folder via `importlib.resources`, renaming `gitignore` to `.gitignore`, refusing to overwrite a non-empty folder (exit 1). Without `--demo` write only adops.yaml and an empty pipelines/.
docker-compose.yml: `shop`, `warehouse`, `dagster_meta` on pinned `postgres:17-alpine`, each with a `pg_isready` healthcheck, host ports and passwords from .env.
seed/01_shop.sql: deterministic synthetic `customers` (id PK, email, updated_at) and `orders` (id PK, customer_id, amount, updated_at), 20 customers and 100 orders.
pipelines/shop_sync.yaml: Sync Step `sync_shop` from Source `shop`, `customers` full_refresh, `orders` incremental on `updated_at`, primary key `id`.

adops.yaml: `dev` Environment with Source and Warehouse, passwords as Secret References; dagster.yaml: dagster_postgres storage from DAGSTER_PG_* env vars; .env.example lists every variable with demo-only values.
Unit tests with CliRunner in tmp_path: demo files written, refusal on non-empty folder, plain init, and the shipped pipeline + adops.yaml pass the domain loaders.
inputs: Demo shop schema and synthetic seed data
phases.expectedResult: `adops init --demo <dir>` produces a demo Project whose `docker compose up --wait` brings all three Postgres services to healthy, with the init code covered 100% by tests/unit/interface/test_init_command.py.
phases.compensation: Remove the init command and templates folder; only the run/E2E phase reads them.

rubric.label: Demo files validate and agree on every variable
rubric.ruleStatement: The generated demo passes the domain loaders, and every environment variable named by docker-compose.yml, adops.yaml and dagster.yaml exists in .env.example, with no literal password in any committed file. 10 = a unit test cross-checks variable names across all three files and the loaders; 8 = loaders pass and a manual check finds no gaps; below 9 is unacceptable because the E2E depends on it.
passCriteria: tests/unit/interface/test_init_command.py loads the generated pipelines/shop_sync.yaml and adops.yaml through `load_pipeline` and `load_project_settings` with no error
A test collects every `${VAR}` in docker-compose.yml, every `*_env:` value in adops.yaml and every `env:` reference in dagster.yaml, and asserts each name is a key in .env.example
`grep -nE "password:\s*[^ $]" <generated>/adops.yaml <generated>/pipelines/*.yaml` returns nothing
`docker compose -f <generated>/docker-compose.yml --env-file <generated>/.env.example config -q` exits 0
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: adops.yaml uses `password_env: SHOP_PASSWORD` while compose and .env.example use `SHOP_DB_PASSWORD`; the loaders pass but the run later fails with a missing secret
dagster.yaml reads `DAGSTER_PG_DB` but .env.example only defines `DAGSTER_PG_DATABASE`

rubric.label: Demo stack comes up healthy with a deterministic seed
rubric.ruleStatement: The demo compose file starts all three Postgres services healthy on a pinned image, and the shop seed produces the same 20 customers and 100 orders every time. 10 = `up --wait` passes, and two fresh starts give identical table checksums; 8 = healthy with correct counts; below 8 = unpinned image or a nondeterministic seed.
passCriteria: `adops init --demo $D && cp $D/.env.example $D/.env && docker compose -f $D/docker-compose.yml up --wait` exits 0 with services shop, warehouse and dagster_meta healthy
Every service image is exactly `postgres:17-alpine` (or a digest); `grep -n ":latest" $D/docker-compose.yml` returns nothing; each service has a `pg_isready` healthcheck
In the shop DB, `SELECT count(*) FROM customers` = 20 and `SELECT count(*) FROM orders` = 100, with primary keys on `id`
`grep -niE "random\(|now\(|current_timestamp" seed/01_shop.sql` returns nothing (fixed `updated_at` literals)
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: the seed uses `generate_series` with `now() - random() * interval '30 days'` for updated_at, so Incremental Sync cursor assertions in the E2E are flaky
Host ports are hard-coded (5432), so the stack fails to start on a machine already running Postgres instead of reading ports from .env

rubric.label: Init never overwrites and writes only user files
rubric.ruleStatement: `adops init` refuses a non-empty target without touching it, creates a missing target, renames gitignore, and writes no tool code into the Project. 10 = all bullets tested, including no partial writes on refusal; 8 = refusal and plain init tested; below 8 = any overwrite possible.
passCriteria: A test pre-fills the target with one file, runs `adops init --demo`, and asserts exit code 1, a clear message, and an unchanged directory listing and file contents
The generated Project has `.gitignore` (not `gitignore`), and it lists `.env` and `.adops/`
Plain `adops init $D` writes only `adops.yaml` and an empty `pipelines/` (asserted by listing)
`find $D -name '*.py'` returns nothing for both plain and demo init
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: the emptiness check runs after the template copy has started, so a refusal leaves half a Project behind
The generated .gitignore omits `.env`, so the user's real passwords get committed on first `git add .`

rubric.label: Templates, including dotfiles, ship in the built package
rubric.ruleStatement: The demo templates load through importlib.resources and are present in the built wheel, including dot-named files. 10 = a test or CI step checks the wheel contents; 8 = verified manually with `uv build`; below 8 = init works only from a source checkout.
passCriteria: `uv build && unzip -l dist/*.whl | grep -E "templates/demo/(\.env\.example|gitignore|seed/01_shop.sql|dagster.yaml)"` lists all four
init_command.py reads templates with `importlib.resources.files("adops.templates")` (or equivalent), not `Path(__file__)` relative paths
Init code is covered 100% line+branch: `uv run pytest tests/unit/interface --cov=adops.interface --cov-branch` reports no missing lines in init_command.py
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: hatchling's default excludes drop `.env.example` from the wheel, so `adops init --demo` works in the repo but produces a Project without .env.example after `uv tool install`

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is a variable-name mismatch between adops.yaml, docker-compose.yml, dagster.yaml and .env.example (or .env.example missing from the wheel); fix it by adding the cross-file variable-name unit test and checking the wheel with `unzip -l`.

phases.name: Add adops run command with Docker demo E2E
phases.goal: Add `adops run <pipeline> [--env dev]` wiring the dlt Sync adapter and Dagster orchestrator into the run Pipeline use case, and prove it end to end with a Docker test and CI job that scaffold the demo, start it, and assert Full Refresh and Incremental Sync results in the Warehouse.
phases.rationale: This is the entry point that makes the slice usable: one command runs the demo Pipeline. Unit tests with fakes cannot prove that dlt, Dagster and Postgres really work together, so the same phase adds the end-to-end test that runs the real demo in Docker on every pull request. It also adds the `e2e` job to the Tool Build CI workflow, because that job exists only to run this test.
changes: Add `adops run PIPELINE [--env dev] [--project PATH]`: read adops.yaml and pipelines/<PIPELINE>.yaml, env = `{**dotenv_values(project/.env), **os.environ}`, set DAGSTER_HOME to the Project when dagster.yaml exists, call `run_pipeline` with DagsterOrchestrator and the dlt Sync adapter.
Print one line per Step (name, status, rows per table), exit 0 on success; on PipelineValidationError, MissingSecretError or SyncFailedError print the sanitized message (no traceback) and exit 1.
Unit-test with CliRunner and fake adapters: success output, each error → exit 1, .env vs process-environment precedence.

tests/e2e/test_demo_sync.py (marker `e2e`): init demo into tmp, copy .env.example to .env, `docker compose up --wait`, `adops run shop_sync`, assert 20 customers and 100 orders in `raw_shop`; insert 1 order and update 1 order's updated_at, run again, assert 101 orders, the update applied, no duplicates; `docker compose down -v`.
Add an `e2e` job to ci.yml running `uv run pytest tests/e2e -m e2e`, required alongside `unit`.
inputs: dlt Sync adapter from phase dlt-sync-adapter
Demo Project templates from phase init-demo-project-scaffold
phases.expectedResult: The `e2e` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml passes on a pull request, running tests/e2e/test_demo_sync.py against the real Docker demo (Full Refresh and Incremental Sync assertions green), while the `unit` job still reports 100% line+branch coverage.
phases.compensation: Remove the e2e job and the run command; earlier phases stay valid on their own.

rubric.label: E2E proves Full Refresh and delta-only Incremental Sync
rubric.ruleStatement: The Docker E2E proves that the second `adops run` loads only the advanced orders rows, applies the update, creates no duplicates, and keeps customers at the Source state. 10 = counts, the no-duplicate query, the updated value and the reported 2-row delta in CLI output are all asserted; 8 = counts, no duplicates and the update asserted; below 9 is unacceptable.
passCriteria: After run 1, tests/e2e/test_demo_sync.py asserts `raw_shop.customers` = 20 and `raw_shop.orders` = 100 in the Warehouse
After inserting 1 order and bumping 1 order's updated_at and amount in the shop DB, run 2 gives `raw_shop.orders` = 101 and the updated amount is present
`SELECT id FROM raw_shop.orders GROUP BY id HAVING count(*) > 1` returns zero rows after run 2
Run 2's CLI output reports 2 rows for orders (not 101), and customers still equals the Source count
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: the test asserts only `count(*) == 101`; it passes even if all 101 rows are re-read and merged each run, so Incremental Sync is not actually proven
The update bumps updated_at to a value equal to the stored cursor maximum, and the test passes only because of an inclusive comparison that also re-loads the boundary row

rubric.label: adops run fails cleanly with no secret in output or run storage
rubric.ruleStatement: Every expected failure of `adops run` exits 1 with a one-line sanitized message and no traceback, and no secret appears in CLI output or in the Dagster metadata database. 10 = each error path unit-tested, and the E2E scans dagster_meta for the demo password; 8 = each error path unit-tested; below 9 is unacceptable.
passCriteria: CliRunner tests cover PipelineValidationError, MissingSecretError, SyncFailedError, an unknown Environment and a missing pipelines/<name>.yaml; each asserts exit_code 1 and `"Traceback" not in result.output`
A unit test with a sentinel password in the fake env and a failing fake Sync asserts the sentinel is absent from `result.output`
The E2E queries the dagster_meta Postgres (for example `SELECT count(*) FROM event_logs WHERE event LIKE '%' || <demo password> || '%'` and the same on `runs.run_body`) and asserts 0
On success, output has one line per Step with name, status and rows per table, and exit code 0
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: known errors are caught, but an unexpected exception (for example a psycopg OperationalError raised outside the adapter) falls through to Typer's pretty traceback, which prints local variables including the resolved env dict
A missing pipeline file raises FileNotFoundError with a traceback instead of a one-line message

rubric.label: Composition root wires real adapters with correct env precedence

rubric.label: E2E CI job really runs, cleans up and cannot pass by skipping
rubric.ruleStatement: The `e2e` CI job runs the Docker test on every pull request, cannot go green by skipping, always tears the stack down, and stays out of the unit job. 10 = all bullets pass and the job is shown green on a real PR run; 8 = configured correctly; below 8 = the test can be skipped or leaves containers running.
passCriteria: .github/workflows/ci.yml has an `e2e` job on pull_request running `uv run pytest tests/e2e -m e2e` with the same pinned actions as `unit`
The `e2e` marker is registered in pyproject.toml, and the unit job's command (`pytest tests/unit`) collects no e2e test

In CI, a missing Docker daemon fails the test instead of skipping it (`grep -n "skip" tests/e2e/test_demo_sync.py` shows no unconditional skip on Docker absence, or the skip is disabled when `CI` is set)
`docker compose down -v` runs in a fixture finalizer or `finally` block, and a unique compose project name per run (`-p`) is used
`gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch <pr-branch>` shows the e2e job concluded `success`
failureExamples: Plausible implementation: the test does `pytest.skip` when `docker info` fails, which is friendly locally, but CI's runner image setup leaves Docker unreachable and the job reports green with 1 skipped test
Teardown sits at the end of the test body, so a failed assertion leaves volumes behind and the next run's Full Refresh count starts from stale data
